cells.tense: You're here with both hands in it — two things that want opposite things from you, and you're giving each of them what it actually needs.
cells.ask: Show one person the thing you've been looking after, and tell them what it's costing you to keep it going. That puts the care you've spent somewhere it can be received, and gives back a witness you didn't have to earn.
cells.core:
On an ordinary day you check on what's growing, you adjust — more light here, less pressure there — and it keeps coming along because you keep showing up for it. You can tell what's ready from what isn't, and you don't force either one. That's the shape of this when it's going well.

You're becoming more yourself by looking after something real, and you're doing it without gripping. You can say what it costs you and still keep going, which is a different thing from carrying it silently. Tell someone what the care costs, and the credit for it stops living only in your own bookkeeping.
cells.sheetLine: You're looking after what's growing, and you know what it costs.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care

cells.tense: You're ahead of it — running the harvest in your head before there's anything in the ground.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're looking after and do the next unglamorous step of it today, in the physical world, before you've imagined how it lands. That brings you back to the part of it you can stand in, and gives back a foothold you can feel under you.
cells.core:
When this is working you tend what's actually there — you can tell what's ready from what isn't, and you let time do its job instead of doing it for time. That's the version that doesn't wear you out.

The trouble is your care has started reaching past today. You're already managing outcomes that haven't happened, comparing them, planning around them — and the things in front of you get your vigilance instead of your attention. You're trying to make the future safe by holding it, and holding it is what's making it heavy. Satisfaction comes from what's been lived through, not from what's been pictured. Do one real step today and let the rest belong to tomorrow.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing an outcome that hasn't happened yet.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care

lint.detail: the ask carries no word of the place — the same ask would serve any seat

cells.tense: There was a place where this was yours to look after, and now you're standing past it with your hands in your pockets.
cells.ask: Go back to one thing you used to look after and do a small ordinary act of care for it — water it, tidy it, fix the one loose part — without deciding anything about its future. That lets the strength you already have start moving again, and gives back the feel of your own hands in it.
cells.core:
When this is alive you're right in it — you tend what's yours, you notice what it needs, and you keep at it even on the days it doesn't reward you. You check on it, you adjust, you stay with it. It comes naturally to you.

The care didn't go anywhere. It just stopped going out. You're still watching from a step away, comparing what you meant with what's there, and the gap has gotten too wide to step back into. One small piece of it is waiting for you — not by pushing yourself into it, quietly, by doing one ordinary tending act and letting that be enough for now.
cells.sheetLine: You still care. You've just stopped putting your hands on it.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care

cells.tense: You're shaping something now — deciding its size, holding one piece steady while another develops — and you're calling it just keeping things running.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to one person, what you're deliberately building and what you're giving up for it. That names the intent already carrying the work, and gives back the relief of holding it as yours instead of quietly keeping it afloat.
cells.core:
A good day here looks like you checking what needs doing and doing it — quietly, no ceremony — and the whole thing keeps moving because you keep deciding how it moves.

You're doing that already. But the deciding keeps getting filed under maintenance, as if the shape of what's growing had nothing to do with you. It does. You chose it, and you choose it again each time you hold one part steady so another part can develop. Say the sentence someone else can hear — the one that starts with 'I'm building' and includes what it costs you — and the work comes back into your own hands.
cells.sheetLine: You're already shaping this. You just haven't claimed it as yours.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care

attempts.check: The claim I cannot support from the record is that Stewardship in this seat is 'about becoming yourself by tending something that grows' — the record only gives me the card's mechanism (decisive cultivation through form) and the seat's meaning (becoming what you are), so the cell must stay with the visible act of tending, not assert an identity. A reader might say 'this isn't about tending, it's about letting myself be seen' — that's the seat's concern, and the cell should not collapse the two. The asks survive being wrong because they name one physical act (show one thing you've tended, take one unfunded step, etc.) that teaches something about the card regardless of status. The sentence that serves the writer more than the reader is any line about 'dynamic balance' — it sounds like the record and would not survive being said out loud.
